body:
## Question

What does opening, switching, closing, reopening, and restoring a project tab mean for its workspace and running work?

Switching views is already required to preserve independent editors, unsaved changes, terminals, Git context, and running work. Decide the remaining contract:
- Closing a tab with dirty files, live terminals, debug/tasks, or an active agent conversation; whether agent execution and editor lifetime are coupled.
- Relaunch/reload restoration, the last project tab closing, and the default view on startup.
- Duplicate project requests, tab ordering, and expected normal and upper-end numbers of simultaneously active projects.
- What attention from an inactive project is surfaced globally, and what remains local to a project.
- The project-local versus global scope of menus, commands, settings/profile selection, and visible status information where the user can observe a difference.
- Acceptable switching delay and resource-use expectations, without assuming a specific hosting implementation.

Use examples of moving between Agents and two projects with unsaved files and ongoing work. The resolution should define observable behavior and acceptance scenarios; implementation mechanics belong to the hosting decision.

comments.body:
## Resolution

Agreed with the creator through two rounds of discussion; all ten recommendations were explicitly accepted. This defines intended product behavior and acceptance scenarios. It does not establish runtime feasibility.

### Workspace and agent lifetimes

- Switching between Agents and project tabs preserves each workspace's editors, unsaved changes, terminals, Git context, tasks, debugging, and running agent work. An inactive project remains open and live.
- Closing a project tab closes its workspace. It does not cancel its agent runs or remove its conversations from Agents. Resources required by an ongoing agent run must remain available independently of the project tab, including any necessary tools or client connections.
- Preserve existing save and Hot Exit preferences. Safely backed-up edits may be restored later; otherwise offer Save / Don't Save / Cancel. A failed save or backup, or cancellation, prevents the close from completing. Never silently discard unprotected edits.
- Confirm before stopping live project terminals, tasks, or debugging. A canceled close leaves the project open. Other projects and agent runs remain unaffected.
- Reopening a closed project restores recoverable editors and layout. It does not restart commands that already ended. Conversation membership and exact workspace matching remain governed by [Define project ownership and navigation for chats](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/17#issuecomment-6456724688).

### Tab navigation and startup

- New project tabs open at the right and support drag reordering. An explicit request for an already-open exact workspace activates its existing tab rather than creating another.
- Closing the active project selects its right-hand neighbour, then its left-hand neighbour if there is none to the right. Closing the final project selects Agents and leaves the IDE usable. The Agents button is permanent.
- Closing an inactive project does not change the currently selected view.
- App startup restores the previously open project tabs, their order, recoverable working state, and the previously selected view. A fresh installation starts in Agents. A project deliberately closed before quitting is not reopened merely because it has chat history.

### Reload, quit, and recovery

- A project reload affects only that project. Preserve recoverable state and ongoing agent work; do not implicitly reload other projects or the shared shell. If active project work must stop, apply the same interruption safeguards before proceeding.
- Quitting the whole app warns when it would interrupt active work and allows cancellation. Agent continuation after project-tab close is not a promise that local agent execution survives app quit.
- After quit or a crash, reconnect to work that actually survived and clearly mark work that was interrupted. Do not automatically resend agent requests or restart tasks. Restoring a terminal shell or buffer is not proof that its previous command survived.
- If a restored local or remote workspace is unavailable, retain its tab with retry and close options. Other projects and Agents remain usable; do not silently substitute another workspace or environment.

### Attention, commands, and profiles

- Inactive projects surface approvals, failures, and completion through quiet indicators. Project tabs show project attention; Agents aggregates agent attention, including conversations whose project tabs are closed. These signals never steal focus.
- Reserve pop-up notifications for actionable requests or failures. Routine output remains inside its project or chat; completion alone uses a quiet indicator.
- Project commands and visible project status follow the selected project: Save, terminals, Git, debugging, and workspace settings target that workspace. In Agents, project-specific actions require an explicit project target and never silently use the last visited project.
- Each project retains its workspace-associated profile, settings, extensions, and theme. Agents and the shared shell retain their own stable profile/theme when switching projects.
- Workspace settings remain local. Profile-scoped setting changes affect all projects using that profile; a profile is not copied merely because multiple projects use it. Application-wide settings retain their global scope. A project profile change requiring reload affects only that project.

### Capacity and responsiveness

- Validate 3–5 open projects as the normal workload and ten as the upper-end workload. Ten is a validation workload, not a hard cap.
- Target roughly 200 ms or less to switch between already-open views. Opening a new project may take longer. These are goals for the feasibility experiment, not measured results.
- Do not automatically close or suspend open workspaces to meet resource targets. Preserve unsaved state and genuine background work. Inactive idle projects should use little CPU.
- Measure memory and CPU during the hosting prototype before setting numerical resource budgets. There is no assumption that ten independent workspaces cost the same as one.

### Acceptance scenarios

| Scenario | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| App has an unsaved file; API has a running terminal/task; an agent chat is active | Switching App → Agents → API → App preserves the dirty editor, each project's context, and all running work. |
| Close App with unsaved changes | Use its save/Hot Exit safeguards; safely backed-up edits can reopen. Failed save/backup or Cancel keeps App open without discarding edits. |
| Close API while a terminal, task, or debug session is active | Confirm before stopping that work. Cancel keeps API open; proceeding does not stop another project's work. |
| Close the project hosting an active agent chat | Its agent run and required execution resources continue; the same chat remains available in Agents. |
| Reopen a closed project | Restore recoverable editor/layout state; do not replay ended terminal commands, tasks, or agent requests. |
| Open an already-open workspace and reorder tabs | Activate the existing tab; preserve the chosen order through restart. |
| Close an inactive tab, an active middle tab, or the final project | Respectively retain the current view, select the right neighbour then the left, or show Agents. |
| Quit and reopen with App, API, and Agents last selected | Restore App/API and their order with Agents selected; recover state and reconnect surviving work without pretending interrupted processes continued. |
| Reload App or change its profile | API and Agents remain usable; preserve ongoing agent work and apply safeguards to any project work that must stop. |
| A restored SSH/Dev Container/local workspace is unavailable | Keep an identifiable retryable/closable tab; other projects and Agents remain usable without substituting another environment. |
| API needs approval or fails while App is selected | Surface attention without switching away from App; agent attention is also visible through Agents. Routine output stays local. |
| Invoke Save, Git, terminal, or debug actions while App is selected, then from Agents | App receives project commands while selected. Agents requires an explicit target and never silently reuses App. |
| App and API use different profiles/themes, or share a profile | Different profiles remain project-specific while the shared shell stays stable. Shared profile setting changes reach both users of that profile. |
| Exercise 3–5 and ten open projects with idle and active background work | Measure warm switching against the roughly 200 ms target and record CPU/memory; no automatic closure, suspension, lost edits, or stopped work. |

### Evidence and handoff

Existing code provides relevant mechanisms, not proof of the combined-window design: `workingCopyBackupTracker.ts` protects dirty editors, `terminalService.ts` distinguishes reload reattachment from process disposal/revival, and `debugLifecycle.ts` handles debug shutdown confirmation. `sessionsService.ts` separates chat presentation from cancellation, while Agent Host residency protects active turns. However, ephemeral-session cleanup, app-level Agent Host shutdown, and client tools tied to a coordinating window mean provider-neutral continuation must be designed and tested. `userDataProfileManagement.ts` already associates profiles with workspaces.

[Choose how independent project workbenches share one window](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20) must satisfy these lifetimes, execution ownership, command targeting, and profile boundaries. [Validate the selected hosting architecture with live workbenches](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/23) must test them, including vetoed close/reload, agent tool continuity, unavailable workspaces, and the agreed project-count/performance targets. [Validate the project tabs and Chats interaction in a prototype](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/21) must exercise the observable navigation and attention behavior with the creator.

These existing tickets cover the newly clarified requirements; no additional decision ticket is needed from this resolution. Architecture, provider support, resource budgets, and platform/remote runtime validation remain with their existing owners. No production code was changed or runtime feasibility claimed in this session.

title: Define project tab lifecycle and background activity
